FBS Tower: illustrative individual-based finite-storage queue model
Levels: Ground=0 to 13. Default population: 1680, of whom 1560 use stairs.
User observation: 11.35 seconds, classroom door to next full floor, one trial.
User estimate: corridor walk 1.5–2 seconds. Derived stair time: 9.35–9.85 seconds.
Sampling these independently adds assumed variation, not empirical uncertainty.
All widths, flow rates, storage capacities, geometry, response delays and exit
layout are unverified scenario assumptions, not code requirements or standards.
11 risers in one flight and 6-inch riser height were reported; a second identical
flight is unconfirmed. Geometry is lumped into segment_plan_length_m=7.1 m.
No metric stair geometry is reconstructed from photographs.

Time zero is a common alert, not ignition. Uniform 0–30 s response delay is
assumed. Each person has one stair-travel time reused on all floor intervals.
Roles are labels only. Base routes use exact per-floor allocation. In the
right-fire scenario, all usual right-stair users are reassigned to the left
stair and receive an assumed additional 8–20 s cross-corridor rerouting delay.
Merging alternates local and upper streams when both are ready. No rerouting.
Each floor-to-floor stair segment has finite storage and width-based admission
flow. People retain FIFO order and cannot overtake. Downstream blockage holds
people upstream. The lowest link also has a discharge flow limit.
At ground, the streams enter a shared finite lobby; final doors are represented
by their combined capacity. Right-stair closure leaves both final doors available.
The red fire-side overlay is a visualization of route unavailability; fire,
smoke, temperature and tenability are not calculated.
This exit topology is assumed and must be replaced if actual exits differ.
No classroom-door capacity is represented. Floor queues are unlimited.
Queue time includes small numerical rounding, excludes alert response and free
travel. Peak floor queues are sampled every 5 s and can miss between-sample peaks.
Per-floor last-person time refers to reaching OUTSIDE, not leaving that floor.

Finite storage creates congestion/back-pressure, but no continuous speed-density
law, body forces, crushing, panic, fatigue, smoke, heat, fire spread, falls,
assisted evacuation, lift use, detection time, or ASET/RSET safety comparison is
included. Do not infer safety, casualties, legal compliance, or actual clearance.
There is no automatic safe/unsafe time threshold in this model.
One-person timing and population conservation checks verify implementation only.
The model has not been validated against a building evacuation drill.
Min–max ranges describe five random seeds under fixed inputs, not confidence
intervals and not uncertainty in real building geometry or behavior.
Animation shows compartment membership, not accurate pedestrian trajectories.

For reporting: Preliminary scenario-based evacuation analysis using an
individual-based queue network under explicitly assumed capacities.
Replace assumptions with measurements before using results for planning.
Background (does not substantiate the arbitrary numerical defaults):
NIST TN 1822: https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.TN.1822
NIST stair movement: https://www.nist.gov/publications/movement-stairs-during-building-evacuations-0
